In these circumstances, the Appellants had approached the Commission by way of two separate petitions bearing No. 1427 of 2018 and 1425 of 2018 respectively seeking energy adjustment with regards to the energy injected into the grid from their respective power plants between 6 th April, 2017 and 4 th October, 2017 along with further 13. The two appellants have assailed the said common order of the Commission before this Tribunal by way of these two separate appeals. 15. A short issue which arises for our consideration in these two appeals is whether the Appellants are entitled for adjustment of energy that was fed into the grid from their respective power plants from the the parties. According to the Appellant these words in clause 5(A) cannot be taken as the third condition to be specified for adjustment of wheeled energy from the captive power plants. It is submitted that the clause specifically provides that the adjustment of wheeled energy generated in the captive power plants would be given from the date of commissioning of the power plants or date of signing of WBA agreement whichever is later. Referring to Section 9(2) of Electricity Act, 2003 it is argued on behalf of the Appellants that right to open access of a captive generator is only qualified by availability of transmission facilities by the CTU or STU, as the case may be. It is submitted that since in the instance case, STU i.e. Respondent No. 5 has, by way of letter dated 27 th March, 2017, confirmed the availability of transmission facility, the only criteria for grant of open access to be was met and, therefore, the adjustment of energy could not have been denied citing extraneous reasons. Reliance is placed upon the judgement of Hon’ble Supreme Court in Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited Vs. JSW Steel Ltd. (2022) 2 SCC 742, in which it has been held as under :- _(I) In case of third party sale / sale to other state, the Power Purchase Agreement will be executed between the Power Producer and the procurer on mutually agreed rates. A separate agreement will be executed for Wheeling of power with Discoms of Rajasthan. The transmission agreement with_ 28. It was argued on behalf of the Appellants that the undertaking has no relevance as the same has exhausted itself. It was submitted that the undertaking was given so that the Appellant could be permitted to Commission the captive power plants within the Financial Year to avail 30. On behalf of the Appellants, reliance was placed upon the two judgement of this Tribunal i.e. Appeal No. 213 of 2023 M/s TGV SRAAC Ltd. Vs. Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission decided on 26 th February, 2024 and Appeal No. 103 of 2021, (Greenko Maha Wind Energy Pvt. Ltd. vs. MERC and Ors., decided on 22 nd January, 2024 to content that power injected into the grid from the generating units without any objection or demur on the part of Respondent Distribution Licensees, even though in the absence of formal LTOA agreement, cannot be said to be infirm and the Distribution Licensees cannot be permitted to evade payment of such power in these circumstances. We find that the reliance placed on behalf of the Appellants on these two judgements of this Tribunal is totally misplaced as they were rendered any absolutely distinct facts and circumstances. In the TGV SRAAC case, this Tribunal referred to Section 70 of the Contract Act as explained by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in B.K. Mondol judgement and held as under :- _the Contract Act, as explained by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in B.K. Mondol judgement, are fulfilled in the present case._ 31. Thus in the said case, this Tribunal found that initially the Appellant was evacuating power into the grid under the valid wheeling agreements which expired on 26 th March, 2016 and 27 th March, 2017 but the Appellant continued injection of power into the grid even after expiry of these wheeling agreements in the hope that fresh LTOA would be executed between it and the respondents for which it had started corresponding with them. Ultimately, fresh STOA agreement was executed between the parties on 7 th June, 2019. In these circumstances, this Tribunal came to the conclusion that it was not a case where the Appellant had been injecting power into the grid in the 32. Further it has been brought to our notice that the said judgement of this Tribunal has been stayed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court by order dated 5 th August, 2024 passed in Civil Appeal No. 8522 of 2024. 33. In so far as the Greenko case is concerned, this Tribunal has held as under :- _“28. We are unable to affirm these findings of the Commission in the impugned order. We have held_ 34. It is evident that in the said case this Tribunal found that the wind power had been injecting into the grid by the Appellant with the consent of the Discom as credit notes were also issued by the discom to the Appellant for some period. In the instant case, there does not appear to be any consent on behalf of the Rajasthan Discoms for injection of power into the grid by the Appellants from their captive power plants. Further, the submission of the undertaking dated 30 th March, 2017 by the Appellants in the instant case makes it totally distinct from the facts of the above noted case, signifying the intention of the Appellants to 35. In view of the above discussion, we do not find any error or infirmity in the impugned order of the Commission. The appeals are sans any merit and are accordingly dismissed.
